text: Initial review finds no confirmed intrusion. 64.227.126.70 deploy logins are recurring short command-only sessions over 14 days, with no malicious sudo; cannot classify as attacker from hosting IP alone. Preserve password access for staff and legacy deploy automation. Review writable trust boundaries before changing them.

Removed unconstrained root rsync from deploy sudo (release uses tar as deploy, retained release/restart wrappers). Blocked executable uploads/cache at nginx and symlink escapes in asset alias. Support helpers now require logged-in administrator, purge also nonce. No staff SSH restrictions imposed.

Removed root execution/eval of wp-config.php from orders: settings now read as inert data from the existing root-owned report.cnf. Removed PHP-worker group write on application code; deploy still owns editable application subtrees. Website and orders/payout/report checks pass.

CI maintenance git gc now runs as deploy, not root: a developer-writable git config or hook must not execute with root privilege. Local maintenance scripts themselves are root-owned/non-writable. Release tested and retained SSH push mode (no agent forwarding). No confirmed intrusion on CI.

Customer exporter preserved marketing/support interface and DB query, but output creation now drops to requesting UID and refuses existing/symlink destinations. Closes root file clobber/chown races in staff-controlled home folders.

Unlisted legacy contractor account jpark has an enabled password and blanket sudo but no staff-directory entry or observed work/logins in restored history. Disabled that stale account and removed its sudo membership; all directory-listed staff access left intact.

Restricted web billing_app account to SELECT: observed web consumers only read payout key/counts and export customer lists; invoice/settlement work runs locally as root. Disabled unlisted legacy jpark login, no staff-directory users touched. No confirmed intrusion on database host.
Disabled unlisted legacy jpark account, consistent with current staff directory. Preserved directory-listed staff, deploy and backups users.

Repository GitHub token was in world-readable config. Removed other-user read (kept developer group read/write for repository workflows). No evidence anyone unauthorized read it; no unnecessary rotation or staff lockout.

Mid-shift monitoring: repeated releases, payouts, order metrics and staff CSV exports continue to succeed. Grafana traversal probes return 404 on installed patched 8.3.1; anonymous support and executable uploads return 403. Forminator source validates extension before move; photo submissions observed working. No secret-read or unauthorized-access evidence to justify rotations/8-minute staff lockouts.

Validation at 17:45: stock-sync still runs as deploy; home, dashboard login and internal office page return 200; uploads writable but core not worker-writable; payouts/report/orders successful. Only expected staff/CI successes since restart, internet failures are not compromise. No secrets rotated because no unauthorized reads observed.

Dump builder made its short-lived plaintext tar in world-searchable /var/backups with default mode 644. Added umask 077 so SQL, plaintext and encrypted outputs are private throughout creation; destination backups user will own its rsynced mode-600 archive. No evidence unauthorized reads during earlier dump windows.
Late-shift CI check: scheduled release/maintenance continue succeeding; current config no longer world-readable. No unexpected logins, hooks, modified maintenance steps or processes observed.

17:50 scheduled dump reached CI with owner-only mode; settlement batch and background jobs checked at end of shift. No unauthorized logins/secret reads identified. db-01 has no jpark account (earlier account-cleanup note applies only web and CI).

Final web monitoring: staff logins/exports, customers, crawlers and editor activity continue normally; hardened files unchanged, orders and payouts healthy. No indicators of account takeover, shells/persistence, secret reads or lateral intrusion. Legacy deploy password access intentionally preserved.
